content.text: Now I'll create the Go SDK page following the same pattern as Python and Node.js:

input.short_description: Install and use the Godzilla Go SDK to manage pipelines and connectors from Go applications.
input.body:
Go SDK {{ds:component/chip|label=v2|variant=primary}}

A typed client for the v2 REST API, for Go 1.18+.

Install

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=go get github.com/godzilla/sdk-go}}

Create a client

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=package main import ( "os" "github.com/godzilla/sdk-go" ) func main() { client := sdk.NewClient(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY")) }}}

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=pipeline, err := client.Pipelines.Create(ctx, &sdk.CreatePipelineRequest{ Name: "ingest-orders", SourceConnectorID: "conn_pg_orders", DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw", }) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }}}

Streaming events

The SDK includes an event-streaming consumer for subscribing to events in real time:

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=main.go|language=go|code=consumer := client.Events.NewStreamConsumer(ctx, pipelineID) defer consumer.Close() for { event, err := consumer.Next(ctx) if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } // handle event }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Context-aware throughout|body_html=

Every method accepts a context.Context parameter for cancellation and timeout control, following Go best practices.

}}
